passages.note: Bill history shows Finchem as prime sponsor of SB1057, a ballot-paper fraud-countermeasures/vendor-certification bill later vetoed; it does not address voter identification.
Senate Third Reading vote page shows Finchem voting Y on SB1057, which concerns ballot-paper fraud countermeasures rather than voter ID.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding any other statute, any vendor that provides fraud countermeasures that are contained in and on the paper used for ballots shall be ISO 27001 certified, ISO 17025 certified or ISO 9001:2015 certified.
passages.note: SB1057's operative text sets vendor certification and anti-counterfeiting requirements for ballot paper; it does not set any voter-identification requirement.

rows.reasoning: The only sourced record, SB1057 (2026), which Finchem prime-sponsored and voted Yea on before it was vetoed, sets ballot-paper anti-fraud vendor certification requirements and says nothing about how the government verifies a voter's identity or eligibility, so it is adjacent to the ladder's question rather than on it.
